description: This program elective helps students understand the difference between low power and high power converters and provides in-depth knowledge of the circuit topologies of high power converters, their working principles and applications.

syllabus.title: Basic Understanding of Converters
syllabus.body: Introduction to power converters, half bridge and full bridge circuit operation, sinusoidal pulse width modulation and three-phase circuits, harmonics in sinusoidal PWM.

syllabus.title: Advanced PWM Schemes
syllabus.body: Third harmonic addition in sine PWM, introduction to space vectors, space vector PWM timing calculation, switching sequence, SVPWM using carriers.

syllabus.title: Multilevel Converters
syllabus.body: Introduction to multilevel converters, cascaded H-bridge multilevel converters, output voltage waveform synthesis in CHB converters, asymmetrical CHB converters, phase-shifted and level-shifted PWM, neutral point clamped converter circuit topology, sinusoidal PWM and space vector PWM, mid-point voltage fluctuations, capacitor voltage balancing, higher level NPC, T-type NPC and active NPC.

syllabus.title: Modular Multilevel Converter
syllabus.body: Topology and operation, arm and cell voltage ratings, arm currents, arm energy balancing, circuit topologies, PWM technique and capacitor voltage balancing, design of components in the MMC, multi-pulse transformer, case study on MMC and CHB, basics of gate driver circuits, turn-on and turn-off process, features of gate drivers and bootstrap functionality.

outcomes: Understand the operation of low and high power converters.
Evaluate the performance of switching schemes for different converters.
Understand multilevel converters and different topologies.
Design and analyze various modular multilevel converters.
textbooks: Bin Wu and Mehdi Narimani, High-Power Converters and AC Drives, 2nd Edition, Wiley-IEEE Press, 2017.
Sergio Alberto Gonzalez, Santiago Andres Verne and Maria Ines Valla, Multilevel Converters for Industrial Applications, CRC Press, 2017.
referenceBooks: Sixing Du, Apparao Dekka, Bin Wu and Navid Zargari, Modular Multilevel Converters: Analysis, Control and Applications, IEEE Press, 2018.
